**Rust:** Rust block comments nest, so `/* /* */` leaves one comment open. That comment hides the `#if 0` line and ends at the `*/` on the next line, `// */`. The Rust `main` then compiles normally. A second `/* /* */` before `#endif` hides the C++ code, and the final `// */` closes it.

**C++:** C++ block comments don't nest, so `/* /* */` is a complete comment. `#if 0` then skips the Rust code, and `// */` is just a line comment inside the skipped block. After `#endif`, the C++ `main` is compiled. The trailing `// */` is a line comment.

The C++ side builds the decimal string by hand, because `printf` has no 128-bit format specifier.
